text.title: CR / BUG Tracking Procedure
text.summary: Six steps: classify the work, allocate the next global number, write the one-page file in the CR or BUG shape, move it through its lifecycle, commit with the matching prefix, and — for a BUG that exposed a missing rule — update project-spec in the same PR.

step.name: classify
step.input: The requested change; the feature lifecycle's current state.
step.action: Decide the stream. A defect against current behaviour is a BUG. A small mutation to existing behaviour or contract that needs a record but no task plan is a CR. Anything that affects multiple subsystems or requires a task breakdown is a feature; a one-line documentation tweak is a straight commit.
step.output: kind ∈ {CR, BUG}, or an exit to the feature lifecycle / straight commit.
step.decision-gate: Not a CR or BUG — stop here and route accordingly (rule skip-this-methodology).

step.name: allocate-number
step.action: The next CR or BUG ID is one higher than the maximum currently on disk in either `todo/` or `done/` (and `in-progress/` for BUGs). Use the shell one-liners in 05-examples. CRs and BUGs have separate counters; never reuse a number.
step.decision-gate: If the computed id already exists anywhere on disk, the counter was corrupted — fix the allocation before writing (rules r-two-global-counters, r-counters-never-reset).

step.name: write-the-file
step.input: kind + id + the facts of the change.
step.action: CR: one page (≤80 lines) with `## Why`, `## What changes`, optional `linked-feature: F0NN` header. BUG: `## Symptom`, `## Repro`, `## Root cause`, `## Fix`, `## Regression test`, optional `linked-feature: F0NN` header. Add the linked-feature header when the change anchors to the feature that introduced the surface in question.
step.decision-gate: A CR that cannot fit on one page is a feature — go back to step 1 (rule r-cr-one-page-three-sections). A BUG without Repro and Root cause is conjecture — do not proceed (rule r-bug-five-sections).

step.name: move-through-lifecycle
step.action: CR: `crs/todo/` → `crs/done/` when the change lands; no in-progress. BUG: `bugs/todo/` → `bugs/in-progress/` while reproducing and fixing → `bugs/done/` once the fix and its regression test are merged.
step.output: File in the state directory that matches reality.
step.decision-gate: A BUG does not move to `done/` until the Regression test section names a real test (rules r-cr-two-states, r-bug-three-states).

step.name: commit-with-prefix
step.action: Prefix every implementing commit: `cr(CR0NN): <short title>` for a CR, `fix(BUG0NN): <short title>` for a BUG.
step.output: Commits that release-notes generators can split into CR / BUG / FEATURE lines without parsing the body.
step.decision-gate: Wrong or missing prefix blocks merge (rules r-cr-commit-prefix, r-bug-commit-prefix).

step.name: update-spec-if-revealing
step.action: Ask whether the BUG exposed an invariant or business rule the project-spec did not capture. If yes, add the rule (`BR-NNN` / invariant entry) to `project-spec/business-rules.md` and/or `project-spec/invariants.md` in the SAME PR as the fix.
step.output: Fix PR carrying both the code change and the spec entry.
step.decision-gate: "Should update spec sometime" is not an option; a revealing BUG without the spec entry blocks merge (rule r-revealing-bug-updates-spec).

list.item: The record validates against the schema in 02-output-contract.xml.
The id is unique across every state directory of its kind and the counter is monotonic.
Commits carry the correct prefix; a BUG has a named regression test before it reaches `done/`.
A revealing BUG's spec update is in the fix PR; the decision tree (06) has been honoured.
